premises.text: Pre-consumer food waste and rising protein scarcity are twin problems that converting waste into protein can address together
premises.evidence_span: if somehow we can convert pre-consumer food waste into protein, we can offer a sustainable solution for both problems

premises.text: A hatchery-and-incubator insect process converts food waste into marketable fertilizer and dried insect protein powder
premises.evidence_span: produces the next generation protein from a specific edible insect by converting food waste into fertilizer

premises.text: The same production system is resource-efficient versus other protein sources on water, land, grain, and carbon
premises.evidence_span: needs minimal water and land, requires zero grain, and almost produces zero carbon emission

premises.text: Companies pay to dispose food waste while insect protein and fertilizer are also sold
premises.evidence_span: Companies pay us to get rid of their food waste. So we get revenue by taking our raw material and by selling our insect-based protein powder and the fertilizer

premises.text: Insect protein powder is denser in protein, calcium, and phosphorus than regular meat
premises.evidence_span: two times more protein, 100 times more calcium, and four times more phosphorus than regular meat

premises.text: Pet B2C growth uses influencers and B2B growth uses pet-shop partners
premises.evidence_span: work with influencers and we also have pet shops as our B2B partners

premises.text: Edible-insect and related rules make the market comparatively easy to enter, including European legality
premises.evidence_span: easy to access due to law regulations

premises.text: Human go-to-market starts with athletes, renal and cancer patients, and people allergic to regular meat
premises.evidence_span: athletes who already use whey protein additional to their diet. And there are renal and cancer patients

premises.text: The insect species is FAO-approved as edible and protein results are certified-lab tested
premises.evidence_span: the species that we produce is approved as edible by FAO

secondary_value.evidence_span: producing much healthier and more sustainable protein sources for humans
